title: The Weight of New Life
verse: She is clothed with strength and dignity; she can laugh at the days to come.
reflection: Nobody tells you how heavy new life feels. Not just the baby in your arms — though that weight is real — but the weight of suddenly being responsible for an entire human soul. You may have imagined this season with soft light and quiet joy, and instead found yourself in something that feels more like survival. You are not failing. You are being initiated into one of the most profound experiences on earth, and it is supposed to feel this big.
prayer: Lord, I did not expect to feel this way. I love this baby and I am also overwhelmed, and I need You to hold both of those things with me. Give me strength for today — not tomorrow, just today. Remind me that You chose me for this child on purpose. Amen.
action: Put your hand on your baby today — sleeping, feeding, wherever they are — and say out loud: 'I was made for you.' Say it even if you don't feel it yet.
journalPrompt: What did I imagine this season would feel like — and what is the hardest gap between that and reality right now?

title: When Night Feels Endless
verse: He grants sleep to those he loves.
reflection: There is a particular kind of loneliness that lives at 3am. The world is asleep and you are not, and the darkness has a way of magnifying every fear and every doubt. You wonder if this will always be this hard. It won't. But right now, in this moment, God is awake with you. He does not sleep or slumber — which means every night feed, every unsettled hour, every time you rise again when you have nothing left, He is right there beside you in the dark.
prayer: God, the nights are so long. My body aches and my mind is foggy and I am running on empty. Meet me here in the dark. Remind me that this is temporary, that You are present, and that morning is coming. Give me what I need for the next hour. Just the next hour. Amen.
action: Tonight, in one of the night feeds, instead of scrolling your phone, sit in the quiet and say: 'God is here with me right now.' Let the darkness be a place of presence rather than dread.
journalPrompt: What does 3am feel like for me right now — and what do I most need God to say to me in that hour?

title: Your Body Did Something Holy
verse: For you created my inmost being; you knit me together in my mother's womb. I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; your works are wonderful, I know that full well.
reflection: Before your baby was born, God was already at work — knitting, forming, knowing. And your body was the sacred space where that happened. Whether you birthed this baby or received them through adoption, through loss and waiting and longing — you became a mother through a holy process. Your body, your story, your journey into motherhood is not ordinary. It is wonderfully made.
prayer: Lord, help me see my body with grace today. Not for what it looks like or what it can do, but for what it has been — a home for new life. Thank You for making me the mother of this child. Amen.
action: Write a two-sentence note of gratitude to your body today. Not about appearance — about what it has carried, endured, and given.
journalPrompt: How do I feel about my body in this postpartum season — and what would it mean to extend it the same grace I would give a dear friend?

title: The Grief Nobody Names
verse: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.
reflection: There is a grief that comes with new motherhood that nobody prepares you for — the loss of your former self, your former rhythms, the version of your life that existed before. Feeling grief alongside joy is not ingratitude. It is honesty. God is not surprised by the complexity of what you are feeling. He is close to the brokenhearted — and that includes the kind of heartbreak that comes from a season of life ending, even a beautiful new one beginning.
prayer: God, I didn't expect to grieve in this season. I didn't expect to miss myself, my sleep, my independence, my identity outside of this baby. Hold me in the complexity of it. Let me feel it without shame. And stay close. Amen.
action: Give yourself permission today to name one thing you miss from your life before baby — without guilt. Write it down. Acknowledge the loss honestly.
journalPrompt: What have I lost in becoming a mother that I haven't fully allowed myself to grieve — and what would it feel like to give that grief space?

title: You Are Not Failing
verse: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
reflection: The feeding that took forty minutes. The settling that took an hour. The outing that fell apart before it started. The day where survival was the only achievement. None of this is failure. All of it is faithfulness. You showed up when you were depleted and you kept showing up, and that is not mediocrity — that is the quiet heroism of new motherhood that the world so rarely celebrates.
prayer: Lord, help me see the faithfulness in my own showing up. I am so quick to name what I got wrong. Teach me to also name what I got right — the love given, the baby fed, the day made it through. I am not failing. I am growing. Amen.
action: At the end of today, write down three things you did well — however small. Fed the baby. Asked for help. Got outside for ten minutes. These count.
journalPrompt: What story am I telling myself about the kind of mother I am right now — and is that story true?

title: Asking for Help Is Brave
verse: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor: If either of them falls down, one can help the other up. But pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them up.
reflection: Somewhere along the way, asking for help became a sign of weakness in motherhood. The ideal is the mother who manages everything without complaint, who never needs anything, who is always giving and never receiving. But God designed us for interdependence. Two are better than one. Asking for help is not weakness — it is wisdom, and it is the design of a God who placed us in community on purpose.
prayer: God, soften my pride enough to let people in. Help me ask for what I actually need — the meal, the extra pair of hands, the phone call, the permission to say I am not okay. Let me receive as well as I give. Amen.
action: Ask for one specific thing today. Not vaguely — specifically. Name what you need and ask one person for it.
journalPrompt: What do I most need help with right now that I have been trying to handle alone — and what is stopping me from asking?

title: This Is Sacred Work
verse: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters.
reflection: The nappy change, the feed, the bath, the settling, the rocking — none of it feels sacred in the moment. It feels repetitive and exhausting and invisible. But God sees every act done in love for this small life, and He receives it as worship. You are not doing small things. You are doing eternal things in ordinary packaging.
prayer: Lord, help me see the sacred in the ordinary today. The nappy I change is an act of love. The feeding is an act of faithfulness. Help me offer it all to You — not as drudgery but as worship. Amen.
action: Choose one routine task today — a feed, a nappy, a bath — and do it slowly and intentionally. Offer it as worship. Notice how it changes the feeling of the task.
journalPrompt: Which part of my daily routine with my baby feels most meaningless — and what would change if I saw it as sacred?

title: Your Baby Knows You
verse: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I set you apart.
reflection: Before your baby could see clearly, they knew your voice. Before they could reach for you, they turned toward you. Before they had words, they communicated their need to you specifically. You are not interchangeable in your baby's world. You are irreplaceable. And God knew this child — and knew you as their mother — long before either of you arrived.
prayer: God, thank You that You knew this child before I did. Thank You that You chose me, specifically, to be the one they know and reach for and need. Help me receive that as a gift rather than a pressure today. Amen.
action: Spend five uninterrupted minutes today just looking at your baby's face. Not doing anything — just being present and noticing them.
journalPrompt: What do I notice about my baby that nobody else would notice — and what does that tell me about the bond that is already forming between us?

title: When You Don't Feel Bonded Yet
verse: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out.
reflection: Bonding is not always instant. For some mothers it comes in a rush in the delivery room; for others it grows slowly over weeks of proximity and care. If you are not yet flooded with the feeling you expected, you are not broken and you are not a bad mother. Love is also a choice made every day in ordinary actions — and God does not snuff out the smoldering. He tends it.
prayer: Lord, if I am honest, the feeling I expected hasn't fully come yet. I am scared that means something is wrong with me. Reassure me. Tend the small flame. Help love grow in its own time, in its own way, without shame. Amen.
action: Do one small physical act of connection with your baby today — skin to skin if possible, slow rocking, singing. Let your body lead where your feelings may not yet be.
journalPrompt: Am I honest with myself about how bonding is going — and what would I need to feel safe enough to tell someone the truth?

title: The Comparison Trap
verse: Each one should test their own actions. Then they can take pride in themselves alone, without comparing themselves to someone else.
reflection: Every baby is different. Every mother is different. And the comparison trap — her baby sleeps through the night, her baby feeds easily, her house still looks put-together — is one of the cruelest thefts of the newborn season. God did not call you to raise her baby. He called you to raise yours, in your specific circumstances, with your particular child's particular needs. Run your own race.
prayer: God, free me from comparison today. Free me from the invisible scoreboard I carry that measures me against every other mother I know. Help me focus on my baby, my family, my pace. It is enough. Amen.
action: Unfollow or mute one social media account today that consistently makes you feel inadequate as a mother. Protect your peace.
journalPrompt: Who do I compare myself to most as a new mother — and what specifically do I fear I'm falling short of?

title: Your Instincts Are a Gift
verse: I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my loving eye on you.
reflection: You know things about your baby that no book, no app, no well-meaning relative can know. The particular cry that means hunger versus the one that means overstimulation. The way they settle best. What calms them, what doesn't. God gave you instincts for this child, and those instincts — tuned through proximity and love — are trustworthy. You know more than you think you know.
prayer: Lord, help me trust the instincts You have placed in me as this baby's mother. When others' opinions get loud, help me quiet the noise and listen to what I already know. You are counseling me with Your eye on me. I trust that. Amen.
action: The next time someone offers unsolicited advice about your baby, practice saying: 'Thank you — I'll think about that.' Then do what you know is right for your child.
journalPrompt: Where do I most second-guess my instincts as a mother — and whose voice is usually loudest in those moments of doubt?

title: The Identity Shift
verse: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
reflection: Becoming a mother is not just the addition of a role — it is a profound identity shift. The woman you were before still exists, but she has been expanded, deepened, changed. This is disorienting. It is also holy. God specializes in new creations — in taking what was and making it into something that could not have existed before. You are not lost. You are becoming.
prayer: God, I feel like I don't fully know who I am anymore. Help me be patient with the becoming. Help me trust that the new version of me — the mother — is still fully loved, fully known, and fully Yours. Amen.
action: Write down three things about who you are that have not changed since becoming a mother — values, gifts, personality traits. Let them anchor you.
journalPrompt: Who was I before I became a mother — and which parts of her do I most want to carry forward into who I am becoming?

title: When Your Partnership Changes
verse: Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
reflection: A new baby changes the geography of a relationship. The things that used to be easy — spontaneity, connection, conversation, sleep, intimacy — are suddenly complicated. Resentment can creep in when you are both exhausted and neither of you is at your best. Love in this season is less of a feeling and more of a daily decision made by two depleted people trying to keep choosing each other.
prayer: Lord, protect our relationship in this season. When we are short with each other, bring grace. When we feel disconnected, draw us back together. Help us be patient with each other's imperfection when we are both running on empty. Amen.
action: Do one small thing today to show your partner you are on the same team — a word of appreciation, a text, covering something they need. Small gestures matter enormously in hard seasons.
journalPrompt: How has my closest relationship changed since the baby arrived — and what does it need most from me right now?

title: You Are Halfway
verse: He gives strength to the weary and increases the power of the weak. Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall; but those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.
reflection: Fourteen days in. You have shown up every single day for this child, and you are still standing. That is not nothing — that is everything. The promise here is not that God removes the weariness, but that He renews the weary. That He gives strength to those who have none. You are not at the end. You are being renewed, even now, even here.
prayer: Lord, renew my strength today. I am tired in ways I cannot fully articulate. But I choose hope in You. Give me what I need for the second half of this journey — and for every season of motherhood that comes after. Amen.
action: Do one thing today that is purely restorative — a nap if possible, a shower without rushing, a walk outside, a phone call with someone who fills you up. You cannot pour from empty.
journalPrompt: Looking back at the last two weeks, where have I seen God's strength showing up in my weakness?

title: Postpartum Honesty
verse: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God. Indeed, the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Don't be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
reflection: The postpartum season is one of the most under-supported transitions in a woman's life. If you are struggling more than you expected — with your mood, your thoughts, your ability to feel joy — please hear this: there is no shame in that. God sees you in the depths of it. And sometimes His care for you comes in the form of a doctor, a counselor, a midwife — someone who can help. You are worth that care.
prayer: Lord, give me the courage to be honest about how I am really doing. If I need help beyond what prayer alone can give right now, lead me to the right person. Remove the shame. I am worth caring for. Amen.
action: Be honest with one person today about how you are actually feeling — not the edited version, the real version. If you have been struggling with your mood or thoughts beyond normal tiredness, please speak to your doctor or midwife.
journalPrompt: If I am completely honest, how am I doing emotionally right now — and is there anything I have been afraid to say out loud?

title: Feeding Is Love
verse: Can a mother forget the baby at her breast and have no compassion on the child she has borne? Though she may forget, I will not forget you!
reflection: However you are feeding your baby — breast or bottle, with ease or with great difficulty — you are nourishing a life. The decisions you have made about feeding have been made in love, in the best way you knew how, with the resources and body and circumstances available to you. God uses a nursing mother as the image of His own unwavering commitment. Feeding is love. However it looks for you.
prayer: God, release me from any guilt or shame around how I am feeding my baby. Help me see it for what it is — an act of love and provision. Thank You that You care for my child even more than I do. Amen.
action: The next time you feed your baby, instead of worrying about whether you are doing it right, say quietly: 'This is love. This is enough.'
journalPrompt: What guilt or pressure am I carrying around feeding my baby — and what would it feel like to put it down?

title: When You Miss Your Old Life
verse: For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.
reflection: Missing your old life does not mean you do not love your baby. Let that sentence settle. Grief and love coexist. You can love this child completely and still miss the freedom, the sleep, the spontaneity, the version of yourself that existed before. God's plans for you include this new life — and they also include joy, flourishing, and a future that holds more than you can currently see.
prayer: Lord, help me hold my old life and my new life with grace. I do not have to pretend I do not miss what was. And I do not have to fear what is coming. Your plans for me are good. Help me trust that even in the fog of this season. Amen.
action: Write a short letter to your former self — before baby — telling her what you now know and what you would want her to know about the season she is about to enter.
journalPrompt: What do I miss most about my life before baby — and what has motherhood given me that I did not expect?

title: Resting Without Guilt
verse: In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for food to eat — for he grants sleep to those he loves.
reflection: Rest is not laziness. Rest is not selfish. Rest is not something you earn after everything is done — because in the newborn season, everything is never done. God built rest into the fabric of creation because He knew that sustained giving requires sustained replenishment. When you rest, you are not abandoning your baby. You are becoming a more sustainable version of their mother.
prayer: God, remove the guilt I feel when I rest. Help me receive rest as a gift from You rather than a failure of productivity. Teach me that caring for myself is caring for my baby. Amen.
action: Sleep when the baby sleeps today — or at minimum, lie down with your eyes closed for fifteen minutes. Do not use that time for your phone. Give your body the rest it is asking for.
journalPrompt: What story am I telling myself about rest that is keeping me from taking it — and where did that story come from?

title: Your Baby Is Shaping You
verse: Yet you, Lord, are our Father. We are the clay, you are the potter; we are all the work of your hand.
reflection: You thought you were the one doing the shaping — teaching your baby to sleep, to feed, to settle. And you are. But your baby is also shaping you. The patience you never had before. The love that cracked your chest open. The capacity for selflessness you did not know existed. God is using this small person to form something in you that could not have been formed any other way.
prayer: Lord, I am clay in Your hands. Use this season — the difficulty, the exhaustion, the joy, the love — to shape me into who You designed me to be. I am not just raising a child. I am being formed. Help me cooperate with the process. Amen.
action: Name one character quality that has grown in you since your baby arrived — however small. Write it down and thank God for it.
journalPrompt: In what ways has becoming a mother already changed me — and is that change something I can welcome?

title: The Season Will Change
verse: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.
reflection: This season is not permanent. The night feeds will not last forever. The fog of early motherhood will lift. The tiny baby in your arms will grow. This is comforting and also, strangely, grief-inducing — because even in its hardness, this season is fleeting. Let yourself be present in it, even the hard parts, knowing it is a season and not a sentence.
prayer: God, help me be present in this season rather than just waiting for it to pass. Let me hold both the relief that it is temporary and the tenderness that it is precious. Keep me here, in today, with this baby who will not be this small for long. Amen.
action: Take one photo today — not a posed one. A real one. The messy reality of your day. Tuck it somewhere for the version of you who will look back on this season with different eyes.
journalPrompt: When I imagine looking back on this season in ten years, what do I think I will wish I had noticed or savored more?

title: You Are Becoming
verse: And we all, who with unveiled faces contemplate the Lord's glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
reflection: Transformation is not a single moment — it is a slow, ongoing process of becoming. Three weeks into this journey, you are not the same woman who started it. Something has shifted, however quietly. The becoming of motherhood is one of the most accelerated spiritual formation experiences of a woman's life. God is not wasting a single sleepless night of it.
prayer: Lord, thank You for transforming me through this season — even when I cannot see it happening. I trust that the difficulty is forming something. Keep working in me with ever-increasing glory. I am not finished. I am becoming. Amen.
action: Write a short note to the mother you will be in one year. What do you hope she knows? What do you hope she has learned? What do you hope she has let go of?
journalPrompt: What is being formed in me through the difficulty of this season that could not have been formed any other way?

title: Held
verse: The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms.
reflection: You spend so much of your day holding — holding your baby, holding it together, holding back the tears when you are overwhelmed. But underneath all of your holding is a God who is holding you. The everlasting arms are not a metaphor for vague spiritual comfort. They are the reality beneath every moment — even the hardest ones. You are held by Someone who never drops what He carries.
prayer: Lord, let me feel Your arms underneath me today. In the moments I feel like I am falling — the moments of doubt, of exhaustion, of fear — remind me that You are beneath me. I am held. I will not fall. Amen.
action: The next time you pick your baby up, let it be a physical reminder: God is picking you up too. You are held as you hold.
journalPrompt: What does it mean to me to be held — and do I actually let God hold me, or do I keep trying to hold myself up?

title: Releasing Perfect
verse: But he said to me, 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may rest on me.
reflection: Perfect motherhood is not the goal. Perfect motherhood is not even possible. What God offers is something far better — His power made perfect in your weakness. Every place where you fall short is a door for His grace to enter. The imperfect mother who depends on God is more powerful than the perfect mother who depends on herself.
prayer: Lord, I release the pressure to be perfect. I cannot do this perfectly and I was never designed to. Let Your power rest on me in my weakness. Be strong where I am not. That is enough. More than enough. Amen.
action: Name one area where you have been trying to be the perfect mother. Say out loud: 'I release perfect here. God's grace is sufficient.'
journalPrompt: What would motherhood feel like if I fully released the pressure to be perfect — and what am I afraid would happen if I did?

title: The Long View
verse: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
reflection: You cannot see the end from where you are standing. You cannot see who this baby will become, what their life will hold, how the love and faith you are pouring into them now will bear fruit in twenty years. But God can. And He promises that the way you start them matters — not perfectly, not without mistakes, but with love and intention and faith. The seeds you are planting are not wasted.
prayer: Lord, help me take the long view when the short view is discouraging. Help me trust that what I am doing now — loving, praying, showing up — is planting seeds that will grow for decades. I cannot see the harvest from here, but I trust it is coming. Amen.
action: Write down one value or faith-habit you want to pass to your child. Then ask yourself: what am I doing today that plants that seed?
journalPrompt: What kind of person do I want my child to become — and what kind of mother do I need to be to give them the best chance of that?

title: Your Baby Needs You, Not Perfect
verse: Which of you, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake? If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good gifts to those who ask him!
reflection: Your baby does not need a perfect mother. They need you — your specific voice, your specific touch, your specific way of loving. And even in your imperfection, you instinctively give good things. You are naturally predisposed to your child's good. God says: if even imperfect parents give good gifts, imagine what I give. Your love, imperfect as it is, is a reflection of His.
prayer: Lord, help me stop waiting until I am good enough to love my baby well. I am already enough for them. Help me give freely, love freely, and trust that my imperfect love is pointing them toward Your perfect one. Amen.
action: Do something today that is simply about enjoying your baby — not achieving, not developing, not optimizing. Just enjoying. Play, sing, sit together in the quiet.
journalPrompt: What gets in the way of me simply enjoying my baby — and what would today look like if enjoyment was the only goal?

title: Community Is Not Optional
verse: And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another — and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
reflection: The isolation of new motherhood can be crushing. The days blur together and the world outside feels far away and the loneliness is sometimes more exhausting than the sleep deprivation. God designed you for community — to be encouraged and to encourage. The meeting together is not optional for a flourishing life. You were not meant to do this alone.
prayer: Lord, bring the right people around me in this season. Help me be brave enough to reach out, vulnerable enough to be honest, and open enough to let others in. I need community. Help me find it. Amen.
action: Reach out to one person today — another mother, a friend, a family member — and make a plan to connect. Even a phone call or a park walk. Connection is medicine.
journalPrompt: How isolated do I feel right now in my motherhood — and what has been stopping me from seeking out the community I need?

title: Surrendering Your Plans
verse: In their hearts humans plan their course, but the Lord establishes their steps.
reflection: You had plans for this season. Maybe a birth plan that did not go as hoped, or ideas about feeding that did not work out, or expectations about what the early weeks would look like. Surrendering your plan is not defeat — it is wisdom. God establishes steps, and sometimes His steps look nothing like the plan, and they lead somewhere better than the plan ever could.
prayer: Lord, I surrender my plan for this season. The way I thought it would go, the mother I thought I would be, the baby I imagined I would have. I choose Your steps over my plan. Lead me. I will follow. Amen.
action: Write down one expectation about motherhood or your baby that has not gone as you planned. Then write: 'I surrender this. God's path is better.'
journalPrompt: What plan or expectation for motherhood has been hardest to release — and what might God be doing in the space where my plan fell apart?

title: What Love Does
verse: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs.
reflection: You have been practicing love every day of this journey — patient love in the 3am hours, kind love in the feeding and the settling, selfless love in the giving up of your own needs again and again. This is what love does. It is not a feeling — it is a practice, and you have been practicing it faithfully. You are more loving than you know.
prayer: Lord, thank You for showing me what love looks like through this season. Patient, kind, relentless, selfless. Let the love I give my baby teach me more about the love You have for me. Amen.
action: Write a love letter to your baby today — not a long one, just a paragraph. Tell them what you want them to know about why you love them.
journalPrompt: What has loving my baby taught me about what love actually is — and how has that changed how I understand God's love for me?

title: You Have Already Given So Much
verse: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
reflection: Think of what you have given over the course of this season. Sleep. Comfort. Your body. Your time. Your plans. Your preferences. Your independence. Every single act of giving has been seen by God and none of it — not one sleepless night, not one skipped meal, not one sacrifice made in love — has been in vain. It is all recorded. It all counts. It is all holy.
prayer: Lord, remind me that what I give in love is never wasted. Even on the days it feels invisible, it is seen by You. Thank You for counting what the world overlooks. My labor is not in vain. Amen.
action: Write a list of everything you have given up or given over in the newborn season. Read it back slowly. Let yourself feel the weight of it — and the holiness of it.
journalPrompt: What have I sacrificed in this season that I haven't fully acknowledged — and what would it mean to let God honor that sacrifice?

title: You Were Made for This
verse: She is clothed with strength and dignity; she can laugh at the days to come.
reflection: Thirty days ago you began this journey in the tender, exhausting, overwhelming early days of motherhood. And you are still here. You have shown up, day after day, for a life that depends entirely on you — and you have done it with more grace than you gave yourself credit for. You were made for this. Not because it is easy, but because God specifically chose you for this child, this calling, this season. Wear it with strength. Wear it with dignity. And laugh — because the days to come are good.
prayer: Lord, thank You for every day of this journey. For the hard days that formed me and the tender days that undid me in the best way. I am a different mother than I was thirty days ago. Keep forming me. Keep strengthening me. And help me laugh at the days to come. Amen.
action: Go back to Day 1 and read your first journal entry. Write a response from who you are today. Notice what has shifted. Celebrate it.
journalPrompt: Who am I as a mother today that I was not thirty days ago — and what do I want to carry forward from this journey into the months ahead?
